original_wisa_caption: The video captures an intense scene on a river where a makeshift raft, constructed from various pieces of wood and other materials, is being pushed by a group of people. The raft is moving swiftly through the water, creating splashes and ripples around it. The individuals on the raft are actively paddling with colorful paddles, trying to steer and maintain control amidst the turbulent waters. In the background, there is a concrete structure with blue barriers, possibly part of a water park or a controlled river environment. The water appears choppy, indicating strong currents or rapids. The overall atmosphere suggests a thrilling and adventurous activity, likely part of a recreational or competitive event.
caption: The video captures a person in a brown hooded top and orange life vest seated inside a low raft woven from dark tubes, floating in churning green whitewater below a concrete spillway lined with blue pontoons. A paddle with a yellow blade and blue shaft stands upright beside the rider, then gradually tilts rightward. The rider's head and torso recline and sink lower behind the tube pile, partly hidden by splashing water as whitewater washes over the raft. The paddle blade lowers toward horizontal and dips toward the surface, while the looped tubes on the right remain the most visible part of the frame. The camera framing shifts slightly while keeping the bobbing craft mostly central.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
